einzeiler: Sam Griffiths on racing the Antrim Coast Half and prepping for Berlin sub-2:20
kurzfassung: Sam Griffiths joins the podcast to break down his recent performance at the Antrim Coast Half Marathon, where he represented Wales. The conversation covers his training philosophy, race-day pacing strategies based on heart rate, and his upcoming sub-2:20 attempt at the Berlin Marathon. They also discuss managing high mileage, injury prevention, and fueling strategies for endurance races.
stichpunkte: Sam Griffiths shares details about running a 65-high half marathon at the Antrim Coast race and representing Wales.
Discussion on the importance of keeping easy runs truly easy to maintain injury-free training blocks.
Sam recounts his experience participating in a unique 50-50 track elimination race hosted by Jake Dearden.
Pacing strategies for marathons, including the benefits of running alongside structured pace groups.
Comparison of training volumes, peaking around 115 miles per week, and adapting to heat and humidity.
Evaluating fitness translation from shorter races and half marathons to predict marathon finish times.
Reviewing pre-race carbohydrate loading practices, including comparing bagel strategies and gel schedules.

clips.hook: Being the slowest runner on the national team
clips.text: The guest explains that joining the squad as the least experienced competitor removed all expectations and created a liberating underdog mindset.

clips.hook: Soaking up the finish line instead of sprinting
clips.text: The runner points out that fighting for a microscopic split second at the very end is pointless compared to enjoying the final moments of a successful race.

clips.hook: Why raw track speed does not guarantee marathon success
clips.text: An explanation is given as to why athletes with exceptional 5k credentials often struggle to match those results over 26.2 miles without specific endurance adaptations.

clips.hook: The mental brutality of floating recovery paces
clips.text: The speakers compare notes on interval training, agreeing that maintaining a moderate float during rest periods requires far more mental toughness than the hard repetitions themselves.

clips.hook: A structured hourly fueling and sodium strategy
clips.text: Details are shared regarding a precise nutrition protocol consisting of specific high-carbohydrate gels and timed sodium intakes to sustain energy throughout a marathon.

Visit lisrunning.com to be coached by us!

On this episode, we had special guest Sam Griffiths on the podcast! Sam has been on a few times - if you aren’t familiar with him I would highly recommend checking out the first episode we did. He has an amazing weight loss to elite runner story.

Sam recently broke 66 minutes in the half at Antrim Coast Half in his prep to a sub-2:20 at Berlin Marathon! We got a full race recap and heard about what he has been doing in training. He recently brought a “coach” on to get some feedback on training for the first time.

Sam uses HR data in a really smart way, interesting to hear about that in his Antrim Coast race!

Enjoy!
